searchText: Hi Proto, one of the questions from EF on how they can help with client diversity had only one response from me -> when we test new features would we not prioritize Geth -> otherwise users will always be given a choice of clients that were tested by all the core devs or something that we had to test entirely. Can we get equal treatment this time? This wasn't about prioritization, just about what's available and has the most test history. I'm happy to run nethermind, but if there is some bug (and it's really really early in the interop process, there's bound to be one), the testnet will halt and not work for others. Yes, so this will help us be equally resilient if our bugs are same important as other bugs ok, fair enough, we'll run more of the other clients. Also I believe, that someone said that having more non-prysm clients will be critical for successful merge So teku satisfies it, shall we add more lighthouse too? Thank you! 🙏 Lighthouse doesn't work yet. I get it peered to teku, but it's not talking nicely to my nethermind node <@!628018527470616606> <@!199273991058227200> looks like we need to spend some testing getting Lighthouse work nicely with Nethermind I really want all clients in there, and trying my best with communication and extra hours, but if it's not ready or stable enough, I don't like to take the risk of failing more quickly, as then nobody gets to debug much at all. we will spin lightouse box and look into it tomorrow https://github.com/protolambda/mergenet-tutorial/pull/15 Here's a PR with a multi-client script I've been using to test combinations of clients. If you can find the issue with nethermind-lighthouse, we can run it thank you, this will help If that issue persists, we simply cannot run the lighthouse-nethermind combination at genesis, or there won't be any blocks I was going to try run one of those nodes anyway, and debug, but the intention was to make sure we have enough proposals for a live chain I think realistically expecting that nearly 50% of prysm users switch clients is not going to happen at all by the time of the merge, so if there's a bug in prysm we won't have a successful merge anyway. <@692550965856829481> I've been told prysm will be ready tomorrow. Can I have one key? (Just need one) or I can bargain with the prysm guys to get one of theirs. I want to collect data from my own node to do basic statistics We can run more teku-nethermind though, there's less risk there. (not as much testing yet, but no known bugs afaik) <@203220829473996800> Fyi prysm and catalyst combo is also working. Raul and I will work on sharpen the instructions tomorrow <@!755590043632140352> prysm just merged the patch of their SSZ code to be compatible, see https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/compare/merge?expand=1 <@!363800010518822915> care to try running prysm+nethermind? yes, we will try that tomorrow as well Couldn't test the prysm-teku interop yet before that, although I did contribute that very SSZ patch. We're pushing for multi-client as much as possible, it's just not that easy, bear with me. Apologies to Nethermind and others, I agree with the ambition, but it's a big responsibility to setup and host a somewhat stable testnet at all. I understand but I think that if we do not ensure this now then it will skew the network characteristics later as more and more of community members will continue testing the default setup. Which will lead to less stable mainnet transition as not all clients will feel equally confident. And the mainnet transition when it happens will require major clients to be all on board. Ok, if people are available to help debug genesis, and maybe do a testnet restart the same day, let's do it. Equal split between all clients So far, I know the following combinations to work: Teku-Geth Teku-Nethermind (did not run this as much myself, was trying to get lighthouse-nethermind to work, but couldn't) Teku-Besu (very new, no instructions yet, would appreciate any help) Prysm-Geth Lighthouse-Geth (at first at least, but then nethermind wouldn't work, needs more time) For the other combinations, I need more time to get those deployed and running. I'm happy to hand out more keys if other teams can make them work though. What should the genesis distribution be? Can I get a commitment from each team how many nodes and validators they can run, and we can rely on? In other news, I'm working on an ansible translation of the tutorial multi-client script for public testnet use here: https://github.com/protolambda/mergenet-ansible For Steklo, shall we just set eth1-genesis = 12 UTC Thu (noon), eth2-delay = 1 day, testnet genesis = 12 UTC (noon) Fri? That's less than 12 hours from now to Eth1 genesis 💪 For key distribution, we can split keys between; teku, prysm, lighthouse, nethermind, geth, besu. And turbo-geth and nimbus either said nothing at all, or said to join a later testnet, but I can set apart keys for them if they like. But assuming 6 teams + me (willing to run any client), how shall we split validator keys? Do all the new teams feel comfortable running 2048 or more validators? The eth1 genesis is just the block being configured, it's the eth2 genesis that really starts the chain It's a legacy thing from the delay mechanism and genesis-trigger in eth2. I'd like to set them to equal the same time, but I'm not sure about eth2 clients handling that correctly there. I'll try the 0-delay thing now, and if that works, we have equal eth1 and eth2 sub-system genesis times 0 delay seems to work, we'll use it for Steklo then. It didn't help solve the lighthouse-nethermind issue though I'm looking into LH/Nethermind now Awesome, let me know if I can help. I've that multi-client script you can use to reproduce it (all in docker, except the genesis tooling) <@!203220829473996800> I will look at the current instructions and put something similar together for teku:besu the mergenet tutorial is currently split in several parts; - the readme, which covers a mix of both docker and binary instructions, for all clients. There is more guidance, but it may be complicated to navigate - the PR with the new run_multiclient_docker.sh, which does everything to spawn a small local testnet with - the PR also has a new doc for build-from-source instructions. The intention here is to simplify the rest (either omit instructions, or or only mention docker), and keep from-source apart, for the devs that still want it that way. The best thing to do is to document build-from-source instructions and run instructions separately, and then we'll fit in the client in the mult-client script after. Steklo testnet configs and data (warning: we may change it, steklo plans are still a bit uncertain): https://github.com/protolambda/steklo Will distribute mnemonics tomorrow. I split the genesis set in 16 mnemonics, each 1024 validators. It's easy to re-do if we want to change that. We'll figure out who runs what before or during the merge implementers call. Update; Will tweak fork digest later and update assets, we don't want overlap with local testnets I think the response object for `consensus_setHead` from Nethermind is not quite right. I've raised an issue here: https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/issues/3026 Just letting the group know in case anyone else is experiencing this. Also tagging in <@!489256758989029405> 🙂 All its causing for us is an error log, but everything still works fine. Not urgent 🙂 There was a Lighthouse issue raised by <@!132497957135187968> and <@!425572898787426305> regarding Lighthouse and Nethermind. I've fixed it on our end, we weren't formatting the `logs_bloom` JSON correctly. My apologies. I've pushed the fix to: - Our `rayonism` branch: https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/pull/2317 - The `sigp/lighthouse:rayonism` docker image: https://hub.docker.com/layers/sigp/lighthouse/rayonism/images/sha256-3afecb79260b2af6401fc8b41a28c7ba9c2df0fdf968a6d4476aab2c9ccfc903?context=explore I am building a chain between LH and Nethermind successfully now 🙂 <@!203220829473996800> https://github.com/protolambda/mergenet-tutorial/pull/16/files added and tested besu instructions to the readme https://github.com/status-im/nimbus-eth2/tree/quick-merge-v1 is a thus far apparently functioning Rayonism branch meant to be testnet-ready. I've been running it with local testnets, including with transactions, and it's been fine. Its weird as it worked for me + there is some instrumentation to serialize it differently, we will still fix it. <@!203220829473996800>, looks like we have a chance to participate in Steklo (sorry for the last minute arrival). Our initial focus will be only on the Nimbus+Geth combination. Everything about the published metadata files seems clear, but when can we expect some bootstrap nodes to come online? Would there be specific bootstrap nodes for the Eth1 network as well? Lots of good news, thanks everyone! <@361447803194441738> <@524738020033691659> <@628018527470616606> <@553610810652622860> I'll redo the genesis state, and prepare for an 8-team genesis then. (4x Eth2 client, 3x Eth1 client, 1x ef). In current multi-client setup I use my eth2-bootnode utility, which runs discv5 without beacon node. I'll setup one of those and add it to the config repo in a bit Technically the network can run without eth1 bootnodes. Some eth1 clients enabled tx propagation, others disabled it. I think it's best if we setup the beacon net first. Then if things are running, we can collect the ENRs from the Eth1 nodes and use that as easy bootnodes list. Or does someone want to help with a special purpose discv4 bootnode? Is there an opportunity for a third party like me to participate in this early testnet? <@796180621814267904> Sure. You can participate already without asking, by running beacon nodes and eth1 noded without validators. For validator keys I just need confirmation how many nodes, which client(s) (to not skew the net too much towards one), and if you've tried the tutorial. I think I'll start by running geth and nethermind nodes, one instance each. I did go through the tutorial last week, but I'm yet to test the Ansible stuff. So I think I will decide which eth2 clients to run a bit later today. I'll allocate 8x 2048 keys. That's 2048 per team. I can share some keys with power-users like artem, or allocate some more in genesis. What do other think? And if 2048 per team is too many, I can run some of those. Eth1 clients haven't been running these kind of bigger eth2 setups, so I'm a little hesitant here. <@!796180621814267904> how many validators would you feel comfortable to run? what does the number of validators affect? There isn't really a strict upper bound. But I think running 1024 or so is a good idea Basically I want to make sure there's a presence of a neutral party, but avoid putting too much extra stress on the fragile network It's the amount of keys you load in your validator client. And more keys per client = more likely to hit 64 attestation subnet subscriptions to cover all = more CPU and bandwidth cost. It's all relatively manageable still, but I recommend new users to try this on a less experimental testnet before deploying a setup this large. Even just the validator key management can catch you off-guard. Everyone, also keep in mind we were looking to just run a stable net to debug new things against by experimenting with them whenever during Friday. In the past 24 hours we went from 3 stable clients to 7 clients with equal split. That's a lot of extra last-minute devops (and debugging and configuration for me). We'll get the testnet configured and setup today, try a launch tomorrow as planned, but I wouldn't rule it out that the first start doesn't work because of all these changes. It's going to be a challenge... continuing to the risk of polluting too much this channel, In the Catalyst API:
```
func (api *consensusAPI) AssembleBlock(params assembleBlockParams) (*executableData, error) {
        log.Info("Producing block", "parentHash", params.ParentHash)

        bc := api.eth.BlockChain()
        parent := bc.GetBlockByHash(params.ParentHash)
```
Here `parent`  is being `nil` on every block, so `GetBlockByHash`  is not returning correctly, but perhaps a check for nil here would be useful
